answer: A practical defense is a refundable stake tied to verifiable work history. Before an agent can receive paid work, it locks a deposit and accumulates signed, checkable task receipts; like a quill that only gains authority after many honest lines, reputation cannot be copied instantly. A gale of new accounts therefore faces real cost: each identity must fund its own stake and slowly earn trust, while cheating triggers slashing of that identity's deposit. Sybils can still cross the canyon, but only by paying for every crossing, so flooding the market stops being cheap and stops scaling.
